body:
Global crypto markets closed Thursday in a constructive tone, with total market cap sitting at $2.72T, up a modest +0.56% on the 24-hour window even as intraday momentum in the majors began to fade heading into the New York close. The Fear and Greed index ticked up to 71 from yesterday's 65, both readings firmly in Greed territory, which tells you sentiment is running warm but not yet at the frothy extremes that typically precede sharp reversals. Volume across all tracked pairs came in at $98.1B, a healthy number that suggests real participation rather than thin-air price discovery. BTC dominance holding at 59.3% with ETH at 11.2% is worth flagging — the gap between those two figures has been widening, and it is shaping the character of this rally in ways that matter for altcoin positioning.

Bitcoin traded at $80,403 as of the snapshot, booking a solid +2.47% on the day and an impressive +10.60% over the trailing 7 days. The 24-hour volume print of $33.62B is robust and consistent with directional conviction rather than noise. Cointelegraph noted that Bitcoin is now eyeing the $81K level as the next near-term target, a move that would be supported by the broader risk-asset bid following Nvidia's earnings beat. The $80,000 round-number level is now the immediate support line to watch — a clean break and hold above $81K would open the path toward the mid-$80Ks where sellers from earlier in the year still have overhead supply. On the downside, a failure to defend $79,000 intraday would be the first credible technical warning that the 7-day move is getting exhausted.

Solana is the headline of the altcoin session, full stop. SOL printed +11.59% in 24 hours and +23.60% over 7 days to trade at $108.1, on volume of $6.91B that dwarfed everything else in the alt complex except ETH. The catalyst is partly structural — Charles Schwab's decision to add Solana to its nascent crypto platform, alongside Avalanche and Chainlink, is a material institutional endorsement that reframes the on-ramp narrative for retail investors who are already Schwab clients. UNI was the second-strongest performer at +9.03% on the day and +22.80% on the week, trading at $4.61, which looks like a DeFi rotation trade piggybacking on broader risk appetite. LINK added +5.64% to $11.88, directly benefiting from the Schwab integration news. XRP at $1.46 put up +5.06%, buoyed by news that Ripple Prime is expanding into US equity derivatives with a Delta One business — a signal that Ripple is aggressively broadening its institutional footprint. ETH's +2.27% to $2,517.34 was the relative laggard among majors, with BNB's +1.66% to $710.73 the weakest 24-hour performer in the tracked universe. The Ethena buyback vote and VC unlock overhaul that CoinDesk flagged may generate incremental interest in the DeFi layer, but it has not yet translated into ETH spot demand.

The macro backdrop is doing a lot of the heavy lifting here. Nvidia's earnings beat is the proximate risk-on trigger, compressing equity volatility and pushing institutional allocators back toward higher-beta assets, with crypto sitting near the top of that stack. Bitcoin's 7-day rally of +10.60% has been specifically noted for pushing mining stocks past AI stocks in performance terms, which is a meaningful cross-asset signal about where capital is rotating. The regulatory picture is gradually clarifying on multiple fronts — MoonPay's new integration allowing AI agents to handle crypto lending on Solana represents the kind of infrastructure layering that serious capital needs before committing at scale. On the darker side of the ledger, the arrest of Poland's Olympic chief on suspected crypto-linked bribery charges is a reminder that regulatory scrutiny on illicit use cases remains active globally, and the UK government's data showing 240 taxpayers each made more than $1.3 million from crypto in fiscal 2025 will accelerate conversations in Westminster about tighter reporting and taxation frameworks.

What to watch tomorrow is straightforward. A confirmed daily close above $81,000 in BTC would be the single most important data point, as it would push the weekly structure into territory that algorithmic trend-followers are programmed to chase. SOL needs to defend $105 on any pullback to confirm the Schwab catalyst is sticking rather than being faded — a close below that level would suggest the move was already priced. Watch ETH/BTC ratio closely: if ETH continues underperforming while alts like SOL and UNI rip, it suggests capital is bypassing the second-largest asset entirely in this cycle phase, which would be a meaningful divergence from 2021 playbook dynamics. Any guidance from Federal Reserve speakers on the September rate decision could reset the risk-off/risk-on dial quickly, and a deterioration in the Fear and Greed index back below 65 would be the sentiment warning shot. The memecoin space deserves a caution flag after the GTA 6 leaker was reported dumping his own token hours before Rockstar's gameplay reveal — that kind of behavior, if it attracts regulatory attention, can create headline risk for the broader market at inconvenient times.
